90	supertype; it now says that the interpreter gives such a type parameter its
91	bound, \TYP{Any} if it has none, and does the same where the arguments that fix
92	a type parameter inside other types have several minimal common supertypes,
93	except a type parameter whose bound mentions a static parameter and one
94	declared with several bounds that the interpreter cannot meet, which it binds as
95	before to the narrowest named common supertype of the arguments' run-time
96	types, a call that fixes one of the second kind failing where there is none;
97	that when it chooses among declarations it passes over a declaration with
98	static parameters whose arguments have several minimal common supertypes in
99	favour of another applicable without coercion; and, until 3~October 2026, that
100	it instantiates at \TYP{BottomType} a type parameter that an argument bounds
101	only from above.
102	The box after the list said that ``The interpreter erases a type parameter that
103	nothing at a call fixes, of a function, to \TYP{BottomType}''; it now says that
104	the interpreter instantiates such a type parameter at its bound, and one whose
105	bound mentions other static parameters at that bound with their instances,
106	except a type parameter that only the bound of a type parameter that the
107	arguments fix mentions, which it instantiates at the arguments' type, and
108	names the type parameters it still erases: one declared with several bounds
109	that it cannot meet, one whose bound mentions the type parameter itself, a big
110	operator's that a reduction or a comprehension does not write, and one that
111	only the result of a function expression without a declared return type
112	fixes.
113	A revision of the interpreter of 3~October 2026 changes the box in
114	\secref{static-arg-inference} once more.
115	It said that the interpreter ``instantiates at \TYP{BottomType} a type
116	parameter that an argument bounds only from above, as a function argument
117	bounds the type parameter of its parameter type''; it now says that the
118	interpreter instantiates such a type parameter at the intersection of the upper
119	bounds that its declared bound and the arguments place on it, with two
120	examples, and still at \TYP{BottomType} one whose bound mentions a static
121	parameter or that is declared with several bounds that it cannot meet, and
122	that a call whose arguments place on such a type parameter two upper bounds
123	that it cannot meet fails.
124	A revision of the interpreter of 9~October 2026 changes the box after the list
125	once more.
126	It said that the interpreter ``still erases to \TYP{BottomType} a type
127	parameter whose bound mentions the type parameter itself, as the big operators
128	$\sum$ and $\prod$ declare theirs, and the static parameters of a big operator
129	that a reduction or a comprehension invokes without its static arguments''; it
130	now says that the interpreter leaves open a type parameter whose bound mentions
131	the type parameter itself and that nothing at a call fixes, admitting every
132	value where it checks a value against that type, what that gives a reduction
133	whose element type nothing fixes, and that it still erases the other static
134	parameters of such a big operator.
135	A revision of the interpreter of 14~October 2026 changes both boxes on it once
136	more.
137	The box in \secref{static-arg-inference} said that the interpreter ``does not
138	yet fix a type parameter by the expected type''; it now says that it does so
139	only at a reduction or a comprehension that writes no static argument and whose
140	value is that of a local variable declared with a type or of a top-level or
141	local function declared with a return type.
142	The box after the list said that the interpreter ``still erases to
143	\TYP{BottomType} the other static parameters of a big operator that a
144	reduction or a comprehension invokes without its static arguments, a
145	comprehension's collection being then built at the type of its elements'', and
146	that an empty reduction whose element type nothing fixes takes the identity of
147	\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and the library's set reductions stop at their first
148	element; it now says that the interpreter instantiates such a big operator by
149	the declared type of the local variable, or the declared return type of the
150	top-level or local function, whose value the reduction or the comprehension is,
151	otherwise by the join of the run-time types of its
152	elements, and where there is none at its bound, or open where the bound
153	mentions the parameter, and names what that leaves: an empty reduction or
154	comprehension that no declared type directs, a comprehension that no declared
155	type reaches, and a big operator whose declared result is not one of the
156	library's three.
157	\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A.
158	The revival decided on 26~September 2026 that a generic call over two different
159	integer types infers the narrowest type that both coerce into, by a rule
160	written into this chapter; on 27~September 2026 that the compiled type checker
161	infers static arguments with coercion and keeps the expected type at a call
162	written as \EXP{f(x)}, with a retry without it so that a coercion of the result
163	still applies, and that the chapter is written with it; and on 28~September
164	2026 that a coercion makes a call possible and never changes which declaration
165	runs when one is applicable without it, the declaration chosen being then
166	instantiated by that rule, that a numeral whose conversions tie is read as a
167	\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and that a \KWD{nat} parameter used as a value converts to
168	\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} as a numeral does.
169	\chapref{multiple-dispatch}, \secref{idn-ref} and \secref{dotted-method-calls}
170	said that static arguments are inferred as \chapref{type-inference} describes,
171	and it described nothing; once the compiled type checker infers them by a rule
172	the text does not state, the text and the implementation disagree, so the
173	chapter states the rule the checker was built to, and the effect below lists
174	where the checker departs from it.
175	The bound in place of the union is the rule by which the dispatcher of the type
176	group's paper of 2019 instantiates a type parameter that the arguments do not
177	fix, the intersection of its upper bounds, never \TYP{BottomType}; the team
178	had assumed the union of the lower bounds, of which the authors write ``we were
179	unable to complete the proofs of correctness'' (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu,
180	``Polymorphic Symmetric Multiple Dispatch with Variance'', POPL 2019,
181	Section~5.4).
182	The paper gives no algorithm for static inference and asks of it only that it
183	never instantiate at \TYP{BottomType}; its one example of a static call is
184	typed at the union of its arguments' types.
185	The revival decided on 29~September 2026 to take the paper's rule for static
186	inference as well, which the paper allows and does not require.
187	The same rule gives a type parameter that neither an argument nor the expected
188	type fixes the intersection of its upper bounds: the paper's solving step
189	``never instantiates method type parameters with Bottom'' (Section~5.2), which
190	answers the question the Working Draft's own note asks, whether type inference
191	may infer \TYP{BottomType} for a static parameter.
192	The reasoning for that item, and for the order in which the compiled type
193	checker tries a call, is in
194	\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/decision-record.md}
195	in the revival's repository.
196	The revival's decision of 29~September 2026 provided that the interpreter
197	follow the same rule where it instantiates a declaration, from the run-time
198	types of the arguments; it has no static return type to add to the bound,
199	except, since 14~October 2026, the declared type of a local variable or of a
200	top-level or local function whose value is a reduction or a comprehension that
201	writes no static argument (below).
202	It departs from the rule for the type parameters that the two boxes name,
203	three kinds by decision and the others as defects.
204	Until 9~October 2026, by decision, a type parameter whose bound mentions the
205	type parameter itself kept \TYP{BottomType}: it has no bound to take before its
206	own instance is known, the paper's calculus admits no type parameter of a
207	method in an upper bound (p.~11:11), and the revival had not decided that case.
208	The revival decided on 8~October 2026 that the interpreter leaves such a type
209	parameter open where nothing at a call fixes it: it does not instantiate it,
210	and it admits every value where it checks a value against that type.
211	An open type parameter is no instance: the rule that inference never
212	instantiates a static parameter at \TYP{BottomType} keeps a call from an
213	instance that admits no value, and an open parameter refuses none.
214	The reasoning is in \nolinkurl{explorations/reviews/p1-judgement.md} in the
215	revival's repository.
216	Until 14~October 2026, by decision, a big operator's static parameter whose
217	bound does not mention it, that a reduction or a comprehension does not write,
218	kept \TYP{BottomType}: it is the element type of the reduction, which this
219	chapter does not yet describe, and from \TYP{BottomType} the interpreter's
220	library builds a comprehension's collection at the type of its elements, where
221	from the bound it would build it at the bound.
222	The revival decided on 14~October 2026 that the interpreter instantiates such a
223	big operator as the desugaring by the type \VAR{N} of the expression would
224	(\secref{revival-reductions}), with run-time types in place of \VAR{N}: by the
225	declared type of the local variable, or the declared return type of the
226	top-level or local function, whose value the reduction or the comprehension is,
227	which is the static return type that the rule above lets
228	constrain the instance, and otherwise by the join of the run-time types of the
229	elements that its generator clauses give, which fix the parameter as \VAR{N}
230	would and so are not the value's type of a parameter that nothing fixes; where
231	there is neither, the parameter takes its bound, or is left open where the
232	bound mentions it.
233	The reasoning is in
234	\nolinkurl{explorations/perf-probes/walk-plain-bound/REPORT.md} and
235	\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md} in the
236	revival's repository.
237	By decision, a type parameter that only the bound of a type parameter that the
238	arguments fix mentions takes the arguments' type: the interpreter has no
239	expected type to fix it, and the library's operator that appends two covariant
240	collections builds its result at such a type parameter, which at its bound
241	would be \TYP{Any}.
242	By decision, a lone type parameter whose bound mentions a static parameter,
243	itself or another, keeps the narrowest named common supertype of the arguments
244	rather than its bound: the interpreter cannot evaluate such a bound before the
245	instances are known, and keeping the candidates it had leaves unchanged the
246	case of a type parameter whose bound mentions itself and that the arguments
247	fix, which the revival has not yet decided.
248	As defects, each gated by an expected failure of the revival's tests, the
249	interpreter erases to \TYP{BottomType} a type parameter declared with several
250	bounds that it cannot meet, having no intersection type, and a type parameter
251	that only the result of a function expression without a declared return type
252	fixes, since it gives that result the type \TYP{BottomType}.
253	Until 3~October 2026 it also erased a type parameter that an argument bounds
254	only from above, taking the lower end of the interval that the arguments give
255	the type parameter; it now takes the upper end, the intersection of the upper
256	bounds that the rule gives, except, as defects gated by expected failures, for
257	a type parameter whose bound mentions a static parameter, which it cannot
258	evaluate before the instances are known, and one declared with several bounds
259	that it cannot meet.
260	The reasoning is in
261	\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-instance/decision-record.md}
262	in the revival's repository.
263	The order, a declaration chosen and then instantiated, is that of
264	\secref{resolving-coercion}, read on the parameter types that declarations
265	declare, as the type group's paper of 2011 reads a declaration with static
266	parameters: it ``is applicable to a type if and only if at least one of its
267	instances is'' (\nolinkurl{Papers/Types/setup.tick}, lines 396--397, in the
268	revival's repository).
269	The numeral's default is what the interpreter did before this change, giving
270	a numeral the narrowest of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} and
271	\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} that holds its value, \library\ declaring their numeral type
272	below \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}; the compiled path, whose library declares its
273	numeral type beside \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and excluding it, took one of the
274	declarations that a numeral left tied, and not always the same one (row~391 of
275	the revival's gap ledger).
276	It is also the Java programming language's type for an integer literal.
277	The compiled type checker gives a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter used as a
278	value the type of a numeral, and the interpreter makes it a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32},
279	so an \KWD{int} parameter is read as a \KWD{nat} parameter is; on the Java
280	Virtual Machine the length and the indices of an array are 32-bit integers.
281	The team's later Types chapter (Luchangco, 2012) gives the coercion relation,
282	the coercion of a generic type and the valid instantiations of a quantified
283	type (\nolinkurl{Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick}, lines
284	938--947, 393--400 and 771--789, in the revival's repository) and never uses
285	the word ``infer''; the type group's paper leaves the run-time inference of the
286	static arguments of a dispatched declaration ``beyond the scope of this paper''
287	(\nolinkurl{Papers/Types/rules.tick}, lines 118--129).
288	The full reasoning is in
289	\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-inference/decision-record.md}
290	in the revival's repository.
291	\item[Effect] A generic call over two different integer types, or over a number
292	type and a numeral, need not write its static argument, and the interim rule
293	of the effect of \secref{revival-numbers} ends.
294	A declared type fixes a type parameter that the return type of a call written
295	as \EXP{f(x)} mentions inside another type, and a call whose result the
296	declared type converts is accepted as before.
297	Where the conversions of a numeral tie, the \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} declaration or
298	instance is taken; where another argument's conversions tie, the call is a
299	static error.
300	A \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter may be a component of a range, as in the
301	specification's own examples.
302	The overloading chapters compare declarations on the parameter types they
303	declare and infer static arguments after the selection, and \secref{type-param}
304	gives a type parameter without an \KWD{extends} clause the bound \TYP{Any}
305	(\secref{revival-overloading}, \secref{revival-bound}).
306	A type parameter that nothing at a call fixes is instantiated at its bound
307	under the expected type and never at \TYP{BottomType}: a call whose compiled
308	run failed loading an instance over \TYP{BottomType}, or failed verification
309	where the call's result was carried as one, now runs; a call with no expected
310	type whose type parameter is declared \EXP{\KWD{extends} \TYP{Any}} is
311	accepted; and a call where the bound and the expected type have no common
312	subtype, such as a type parameter bounded by \TYP{Object} where \TYP{()} is
313	expected, is a static error unless the result of the instance at the bound
314	converts to the expected type.
315	The compiled type checker departed from the chapter in five cases, each gated
316	by an expected failure of its tests, until it was revised with the item above:
317	the expected type could let a declaration applicable only with coercion be
318	chosen over a declaration with static parameters that is applicable without it
319	(row~508 of the revival's gap ledger); a call that the rule instantiates at the
320	bound, with another argument converted, was refused (row~515); a type parameter
321	declared without an \KWD{extends} clause, which has no narrowest candidate, was
322	instantiated at the union of the arguments' types where the chapter gives
323	\TYP{Any} (row~516); an argument that is an instance at a union, which only the
324	checker's own union made, was refused where it fixes a type parameter
325	(row~518); and an argument whose static type is an intersection, which the
326	typing of a call between two traits with \KWD{comprises} clauses gives
327	(\secref{revival-meet}), fixed a type parameter at one of its conjuncts
328	(row~541).
329	It now follows the chapter in each, trying a call by subtyping without the
330	expected type first and keeping that attempt when its result converts to the
331	expected type, and the five tests are plain tests of the rule.
332	The compiled path's run time does not yet load an instance at an intersection
333	type (row~559), which the rule gives by two routes: an argument whose static
334	type is an intersection, as in the last of them, and a type parameter that
335	nothing at a call fixes whose declared bound and expected type are two traits
336	that meet at their intersection.
337	A program that the compiled path ran before this revision, at one conjunct of
338	such an intersection or at \TYP{BottomType}, now dies loading that instance.
339	A written bound, such as \TYP{Number}, is taken by both implementations where
340	the chapter gives it.
341	Under the interpreter, a type parameter that nothing at a call fixes runs at its
342	bound where it ran at \TYP{BottomType}, and a type parameter with no narrowest
343	candidate at its bound where it ran at the arguments' narrowest named common
344	supertype, except the type parameters that the boxes on the interpreter name;
345	a call whose arguments have several minimal common supertypes runs where it
346	stopped the interpreter, unless they fix a type parameter declared with several
347	bounds that the interpreter cannot meet or one whose bound mentions the type
348	parameter itself.
349	Since 3~October 2026, under the interpreter, a type parameter that an argument
350	bounds only from above runs at the intersection of its upper bounds where it ran at
351	\TYP{BottomType}, except the type parameters that the box in
352	\secref{static-arg-inference} names; a call whose arguments place on such a
353	type parameter two upper bounds that the interpreter cannot meet, as functions
354	of two traits neither of which extends the other do, still fails with an error
355	of unification, as it failed before (row~616 of the revival's gap ledger).
356	Since 9~October 2026, under the interpreter, a type parameter whose bound
357	mentions the type parameter itself and that nothing at a call fixes is left

=== XXXGenericBoundsNoMeetWalk.fss
component XXXGenericBoundsNoMeetWalk
export Executable

(* Two generic declarations over ListI[P], one with P bounded by A and one by B, overlap at every ListI[P] with P below both, and no declaration covers the overlap, so the program is refused at load, under walk (overloading.tex, section "Declarations with Static Parameters"). *)

trait A end
trait B end
trait C extends { A, B } end
object ListI[\X\] end
object SortedListI[\X\] end

sort[\P extends A\](x: ListI[\P\]): SortedListI[\P\] = SortedListI[\P\]
sort[\P extends B\](x: ListI[\P\]): SortedListI[\P\] = SortedListI[\P\]

run(): () = do
    println(sort(ListI[\C\]))
    println("ran")
  end

end
--- XXXGenericBoundsNoMeetWalk.test
load_exception_contains=at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types
=== XXXNoDuplicatesRuleWalk.fss
component XXXNoDuplicatesRuleWalk
export Executable

(* Two generic declarations whose parameter types Box[T] and Box[U] are each as specific as the other break the No Duplicates Rule, so the program is refused at load, under walk (overloading.tex, section "Declarations with Static Parameters"). *)

object Box[\T\] end

dup[\T\](x: Box[\T\]): ZZ32 = 1
dup[\U\](x: Box[\U\]): ZZ32 = 2

run(): () = do
    println(dup(Box[\String\]))
  end

end
--- XXXNoDuplicatesRuleWalk.test
load_exception_contains=at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types
=== XXXIfClauseObjectWalk.fss
component XXXIfClauseObjectWalk
export Executable

(* An if clause without a binding whose value is an object that is not a Boolean is a static error, so the program is refused at load, under walk (if.tex, section "If Expressions"). *)

object O end

chosen: String = if O then "then" else "else" end

run(): () = println(chosen)

end
--- XXXIfClauseObjectWalk.test
load_exception_contains=If clause did not return boolean
=== XXXUserBigOperatorResultTraitWalk.fss
component XXXUserBigOperatorResultTraitWalk
import List.{...}
export Executable

(* A reduction with no static argument over a user big operator whose declared result is a trait of its own extending BigOperator is directed by the type of its body, as one declared BigReduction is. *)

object CatReduction[\T\] extends MonoidReduction[\List[\T\]\]
    getter asString(): String = "cat"
    empty(): List[\T\] = <|[\T\] |>
    join(a: List[\T\], b: List[\T\]): List[\T\] = a || b
end

trait CatOperator[\T\] extends BigOperator[\List[\T\],List[\T\],List[\T\],List[\T\]\] end

object Cat[\T\] extends CatOperator[\T\]
    getter reduction(): ActualReduction[\List[\T\],List[\T\]\] = CatReduction[\T\]
    getter body(): List[\T\]->List[\T\] = fn (x: List[\T\]): List[\T\] => x
    getter unwrap(): List[\T\]->List[\T\] = fn (x: List[\T\]): List[\T\] => x
end

opr BIG CATOP[\T\](): CatOperator[\T\] = Cat[\T\]

run(): () = do
    c = BIG CATOP[k <- 0#3] <|[\ZZ32\] k|>
    assert(c, <|[\ZZ32\] 0, 1, 2|>, "BIG CATOP of the lists <|k|> over 0#3, each a List[ZZ32], is their concatenation, the big operator's static argument being fixed by the type of the body (reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\"; defining-generators.tex, subsection \"Simple Desugaring of Expressions with Generators\")")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

************************************************************)

(* This makes excludes work without where clauses, and allows opr =()
   to remain non-parametric. *)
value trait AnyMaybe extends { AnyUniqueItem } excludes Number
        (** \vspace{-4ex} NOT YET: %comprises Maybe[\T\] where [\T\]% *)
    opr =(self, other:AnyMaybe): Boolean = self SEQV other
end

just(t:Any):AnyMaybe = Just(t)

(** %Maybe% represents either %Nothing% or a single element of type
    %T% (%Just[\T\]%), which may be retrieved by calling %get%.  An
    object of type %Maybe[\T\]% can be used as a generator; it is either
    empty (%Nothing%) or generates the single element yielded by
    %get%, so there is no issue of canonical order or parallelism.

    Thus, %Just[\T\]% can be used as a single-element generator, and
    %Nothing% can be used as an empty generator. *)
value trait Maybe[\T\]
        extends { AnyMaybe, Condition[\T\], UniqueItem[\T\] }
        comprises { Nothing[\T\], Just[\T\] }
    opr SQCAP(self, o: Maybe[\T\]): Maybe[\T\] = Nothing[\T\]    (*) semilattice "meet" operator
    map[\G\](f: T->G): Maybe[\G\] =
        cond[\Maybe[\G\]\](fn (e:T):Maybe[\G\] => Just[\G\](f(e)), fn ():Maybe[\G\] => Nothing[\G\])
    ivmap[\G\](f: (ZZ32,T)->G): Maybe[\G\] =
        cond[\Maybe[\G\]\](fn (e:T):Maybe[\G\] => Just[\G\](f(0,e)), fn ():Maybe[\G\] => Nothing[\G\])
end

value object Just[\T\](x:T) extends Maybe[\T\]
    getter size()=1
    getter asString():String = "Just(" x ")"
    getter holds() = true
    getter get() = x
    opr |self| : ZZ32 = 1
    getDefault(_:T): T = x
    cond[\R\](t:T->R, _:()->R): R = t(x)
    generate[\R\](_:Reduction[\R\],m:T->R): R = m(x)
    opr[i:ZZ32]:T = if i=0 then x else fail("Maybe[" i "] nonzero index") end

    map[\G\](f: T->G): Just[\G\] = Just[\G\](f(x))
    cross[\G\](g: Generator[\G\]): Generator[\(T,G)\] =
        g.map[\(T,G)\](fn (e:G):(T,G) => (x,e))

    mapReduce[\R\](m: T->R, _:(R,R)->R, _:R): R = m(x)
    reduce(_:(T,T)->T, _:T):T = x
    reduce(_: Reduction[\T\]):T = x
    loop(f:T->()): () = f(x)
    opr IN(y:T, self): Boolean = x=y

cat > GenericPairExcludingWalk.fss <<'EOF'
component GenericPairExcludingWalk
export Executable

(* Two generic declarations whose domains exclude over all their instances, or one of which lies inside the other, are a valid overloading, and each call runs the declaration its argument's type selects (overloading.tex, sections "Declarations with Static Parameters" and "Overloading Resolution"). *)

object Red end
object Blue end
object Box[\T\](v: T) end
object Crate[\T\](v: T) end
trait Tag[\X\] end
trait Sub[\X\] extends Tag[\X\] end
object TagBlue extends Tag[\Blue\] end
object SubBlue extends Sub[\Blue\] end

take[\T\](x: Box[\T\]): String = "box"
take[\T\](x: Crate[\T\]): String = "crate"

tint[\T extends Red\](x: Box[\T\]): String = "red"
tint[\T extends Blue\](x: Box[\T\]): String = "blue"

mark[\T\](x: Box[\T\], y: Red): String = "box and red"
mark[\T\](x: Box[\T\], y: Blue): String = "box and blue"

pick[\T\](x: Box[\T\]): String = "any box"
pick[\U extends Red\](x: Box[\U\]): String = "red box"

kind[\X\](t: Tag[\X\]): String = "tag"
kind[\X\](t: Sub[\X\]): String = "sub"

run(): () = do
    assert(take(Box[\ZZ32\](1)), "box", "Box and Crate are two generic objects, so their instances exclude")
    assert(take(Crate[\ZZ32\](1)), "crate", "a Crate runs the declaration over Crate")
    assert(tint(Box[\Red\](Red)), "red", "the bounds Red and Blue exclude, so no Box instance is in both domains")
    assert(tint(Box[\Blue\](Blue)), "blue", "a Box of Blue runs the declaration bounded by Blue")
    assert(mark(Box[\ZZ32\](1), Red), "box and red", "the second parameters Red and Blue exclude")
    assert(mark(Box[\ZZ32\](1), Blue), "box and blue", "a Blue second argument runs the declaration over Blue")
    assert(pick(Box[\Red\](Red)), "red box", "a Box of Red runs the declaration whose domain lies inside the other's (overloading.tex, section \"Overloading Resolution\")")
    assert(pick(Box[\Blue\](Blue)), "any box", "a Box of Blue runs the unbounded declaration")
    assert(kind(SubBlue), "sub", "a Sub runs the declaration over Sub, which lies inside the one over Tag")
    assert(kind(TagBlue), "tag", "a Tag that is no Sub runs the declaration over Tag")
    println("PASS")
  end

end
EOF
